subtitle: Cultural frameworks can help you ask better questions and understand meanings. Use them responsibly, keeping real people, evidence and your responsibilities in view.
scope: For staff across DHS. Framework concepts and original learning examples support cultural understanding; they do not classify an individual, reproduce a proprietary assessment or decide a personnel, service or policy outcome. The official IDC has five orientations ending in Adaptation; in this program, Integration means the people a process affects help design it, and it is not an added official IDC orientation. Actual information, reporting and decision responsibilities remain. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the person or area responsible within ADSA.
introTranscript: A cultural framework can help you notice a question you might otherwise miss. It becomes less useful when its categories replace the person’s account or turn one exchange into a judgment about a group. Follow Noor and Vale as they prepare a practice memory book, compare learned meanings and use several frameworks for different questions. You can learn with the example or reflect privately without entering a cultural history or producing a work result.

intro.heading: Begin with the question, not the category
intro.body:
Noor and Vale are making a practice memory book for an older neighbor, Ellis. Noor proposes arranging the photographs by year. Vale proposes arranging them around relationships and shared occasions. Both say they want the book to honor Ellis. Noor starts to call Vale “relationship-oriented,” while Vale starts to call Noor “rigidly task-oriented.” The project has two proposed arrangements, but it has not established either person’s cultural type or Ellis’s preference.

A useful first question is what each arrangement signifies to its proposer. Does chronological order honor an unfolding life? Does placing people together express continuing connection? Or do the characters have other reasons? Those are possible questions, not answers supplied by appearance, name or a framework label. Ellis may also prefer a different arrangement entirely.

A framework can help someone recognize that an ordinary design choice may carry learned meanings. It does not remove the need to hear the actual person or check the relevant facts. Here, using a lens should help Noor and Vale understand the purpose behind the order, not prove which person is more culturally developed or give either authority over Ellis’s story.

The Council of Europe describes cultures as internally varied and used in personal, changing ways. That concept challenges a category-first response. Multiple affiliations and experiences can matter, and not every difference in a project is cultural. The inquiry should remain open to a practical preference, a learned value or something else the person explains.

You may privately consider a familiar way of honoring someone or use the full fiction. Learning why a particular arrangement feels respectful to you is worthwhile without sharing family history or finishing a book. First notice the question the situation actually raises.

items.title: Identify what needs understanding
items.body: Noor and Vale have different proposals but the same stated purpose. Asking what each arrangement honors makes the inquiry more precise. A label such as “rigid” would skip that explanation and make an ordinary design difference sound like a settled character problem.

items.title: Use a lens to widen attention
items.body: A cultural lens may draw attention to learned meanings of time, relationship or regard. It can suggest a question about the book’s order. It cannot establish that these meanings apply until the characters explain them; the lens opens inquiry rather than fills in a missing personal account.

items.title: Keep the recipient’s choice visible
items.body: The book is for Ellis, whose preference is not yet known. Understanding the contributors does not make either proposal the correct choice for the recipient. The inquiry should include what Ellis wants, without turning appreciation for a gift into a requirement to accept its proposed design.

tabs.label: A category as the answer
tabs.body: Noor calls Vale relationship-oriented and assumes the book must use relationship sections. The category seems efficient but does not explain Vale’s purpose or Ellis’s choice. It makes the framework stand in for information the project still needs.

tabs.label: No inquiry because the goal is shared
tabs.body: Vale says everyone wants to honor Ellis, so the different proposals do not need discussion. The shared purpose matters, yet it does not explain how either arrangement carries that purpose. A common goal can coexist with meanings worth understanding.

tabs.label: A defined learning question
tabs.body: They ask what each arrangement would honor and how Ellis wants to use the book. This keeps the purpose and individual accounts central. A framework may help them notice an overlooked meaning without deciding a person’s type or the final arrangement.

check.question: What is a useful first question here?
check.correct: What does each proposed arrangement mean to its proposer, and what does Ellis want from the book?
wrong: Which contributor has the higher cultural score based on the arrangement?
Which cultural category must Ellis accept because a gift is being offered?
Why should one shared purpose make all differences irrelevant?
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The question opens understanding and preserves the recipient’s preference without a personal label or inferred score.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A design proposal does not establish a cultural score. A gift does not require the recipient to accept a category or arrangement. A shared purpose also does not explain every difference. Ask about the meaning and desired use before making a conclusion.

intro.heading: Compare meanings without turning them into group rules
intro.body:
Noor explains that in earlier family memory projects, dates helped show the effort and changes across a person’s life. Placing a first garden beside later harvests honored what the person learned over time. Noor’s chronology proposal is meant to recognize a life’s development, not simply to finish a task quickly.

Vale explains that a neighborhood remembrance group arranged photographs by the people and occasions that continued to connect them. A person who had moved away could appear beside a recent gathering because the connection still mattered. Vale’s relationship sections are meant to honor continuing belonging, not to make dates unimportant. These are the characters’ supplied learned meanings, with particular experiences behind them.

They can now reconsider their initial labels. Noor can see that Vale’s order has a coherent purpose rather than being a disorganized refusal of accuracy. Vale can see that chronology expresses regard rather than lack of care for relationships. Neither account proves that every family prefers dates or every neighborhood group prefers relationship sections. A comparative question can reveal a difference without turning it into a national or personal profile.

Their understanding also leaves practical information intact. A caption should not invent a date or identify someone incorrectly. They might combine accurate captions with relationship sections, or offer Ellis a choice of arrangements. The possible combination arises from these stated purposes and facts; it is not a universal solution selected by the course. Ellis’s preference still matters.

Privately examine a practice whose meaning you previously treated as obvious, or stay with the full example. You can gain understanding of your own learned regard without choosing a cultural category, sharing an identity or applying the idea in agency work.

items.title: Explain the purpose behind the form
items.body: Noor connects dates to a life’s unfolding effort, while Vale connects sections to continuing belonging. These purposes give the design choices more depth than task-versus-relationship labels. A useful contrast examines what the forms convey rather than ranks the contributors’ worth.

items.title: Use the account at its actual scope
items.body: The example supplies experiences from a family project and a remembrance group. It does not establish everyone’s approach within either setting. Another member might explain a different meaning. Keep the particular story informative without converting it into a community rule.

items.title: Separate interpretation from accurate details
items.body: Understanding belonging does not authorize an invented caption, and chronology does not prove the whole design is right. A choice about layout can coexist with reliable dates and names. The contributors can consider a combined option while remaining open to Ellis’s desired use.

tabs.label: A binary picture of people
tabs.body: The contrast becomes “all family-oriented people use dates; all community-oriented people use relationships.” This incorrectly turns two stories into two populations. It can hide variation and other purposes, including the recipient’s preference. Keep the comparison tied to the actual meanings the people describe.

tabs.label: A more generous individual interpretation
tabs.body: Each person recognizes a form of regard in the other proposal. The perspective shift removes an earlier unsupported judgment without requiring either to abandon a valued practice. It can matter personally even if the project ultimately uses only one arrangement.

tabs.label: A combined option without a guarantee
tabs.body: Accurate captions inside relationship sections might recognize parts of both purposes. That is an option to discuss, not proof every conflict can be solved by combining designs. Ellis may prefer chronology or something else; the comparison informs rather than dictates the choice.

check.question: What does the comparison establish?
check.correct: Noor and Vale explain two particular learned meanings that help reinterpret their proposals, while group patterns and Ellis’s preference remain separate questions.
wrong: Every member of Noor’s family values chronology over relationships.
Vale’s neighborhood experience makes captions and dates unnecessary.
The combined design is required for every intercultural disagreement.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The particular accounts improve interpretation without a group script, inaccurate record or universal solution.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An individual account cannot establish every family member’s values. A relationship purpose does not erase accurate captions, and a possible combination is not a required response to every disagreement. Keep the meanings and options at the scope the example supports.

Vale connects relationship sections with continuing belonging.
Ask Ellis whether accurate captions within relationship sections would help.
Offer an accurate chronological layout for Ellis to consider.
Everyone in the family values the same arrangement.
Combining designs always resolves cultural disagreement.

intro.heading: Use these learning practices for different learning questions
intro.body:
Cultural intelligence in this program is a broad, multidisciplinary practice. Sociology, anthropology, psychology, communication, education and other fields offer different lenses; disability justice, person-centered practice, intercultural development, psychological safety and lived experience offer further perspectives. Examine access, institutional rules, power and whose knowledge is heard. No single model defines the whole program. This example uses curiosity, contextual understanding, planning and response as useful questions, not a score or an IDI placement.

In the memory-book fiction, a curiosity question might ask what makes Noor curious enough to understand Vale’s purpose rather than dismiss it. A understanding question might ask what Noor has learned about the supplied belonging meaning and how it differs from chronology’s meaning. A planning question might ask how to present accurate options to Ellis without assuming the recipient shares either history. An response question might ask how Noor will describe and offer those options differently. These are original illustrative applications, not assessment items.

The shift can be concrete. Noor first wanted to insist on dates as the only respectful arrangement. After hearing Vale, Noor can describe the relationship option accurately and ask Ellis how the book should be used. The response changes because the meaning has been understood, not merely because a template was handed over. Noor still cares about correct names and dates.

One good response does not supply a cultural intelligence result, establish a permanent capability or authorize a personnel judgment. Conversely, a hesitant response is not proof of a low capability. Practice can reveal a question to work on without becoming a scorecard. You can examine the four different questions privately with the example and choose the one most useful now. No sensitive reflection or formal assessment needs to be entered here.

Use these questions to examine your own habits, your team and your process: Whose goals does my usual plan assume it is serving, and does my form favor self-direction? Who feels able to say no to me, and what does my position do to that? How much do I need settled before I act, and what does a vague notice from me do to people? Do I build trust through results first, or through care first? Is my timeline, or my funder’s, shorter than the problem? How much do I leave unsaid, and who is shut out by my acronyms? Do I count it against someone who leaves early for family? Do I reach first for one rule for everyone or for the case in front of me, and how do I answer a colleague who objects on the other ground? Am I reading how much someone shows as how much they feel, when flat affect or a speech difference may be part of the picture? Does my deadline treat other uses of time as laziness, and have I checked a missed appointment against shift, bus, cost and rule first?

items.title: Keep the capabilities distinct
items.body: Curiosity about Vale’s meaning, understanding that meaning, planning a choice and changing the presentation concern different parts of the learning. One can inform another without being identical. Calling all of them “awareness” loses the useful distinction between wanting to learn and actually responding differently.

items.title: Make a question rather than a rating
items.body: “What do I still need to understand about this order?” is a practical understanding question. “Vale scored highly because of the layout” is an unsupported rating. The course uses public concepts to support inquiry; it does not reproduce the provider’s assessment or establish an individual result.

items.title: Connect understanding and response
items.body: Noor’s revised presentation offers a relationship arrangement as a coherent expression of regard. This follows learning about belonging. Merely changing a font or copying a diagram would not show that connection. A suitable changed act reflects the meaning learned while preserving accurate captions and Ellis’s choice.

tabs.label: Memorize the four names only
tabs.body: Remembering curiosity, contextual understanding, planning and response helps orient the learner, but the list alone does not explain the memory-book exchange. Ask which question each concept brings into view. The terminology is useful when it helps understand and respond, rather than becoming another task to perform for its own sake.

tabs.label: Make a homemade cultural intelligence score
tabs.body: Awarding points for a particular layout or a single question invents a personal measure the course cannot validate. It also confuses the learning application with the provider’s actual assessment. Keep a specific practice observation separate from any individual cultural intelligence result or employment record.

tabs.label: Choose the relevant question
tabs.body: A learner may focus on curiosity, a missing meaning, a plan or a suitable response according to the present situation. Noor’s case benefits from linking Vale’s account to the offered options. This supports a focused next step without demanding all four in every conversation.

check.question: How can the cultural intelligence concepts help in this example?
check.correct: They can guide distinct questions about curiosity, understanding, planning and an appropriate response without generating a personal assessment score.
wrong: They assign four new IDC orientations to Noor and Vale.
They produce a validated personnel score from the selected book layout.
They guarantee Ellis will approve any design called culturally intelligent.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The concepts guide learning while the application remains distinct from assessment and outcome prediction.
check.feedbackIncorrect: These learning practices are not IDC orientations. A layout cannot establish a validated personnel score, and using a framework does not guarantee the recipient’s approval. Apply the relevant learning question to the actual meaning and situation.

items.text: Thoughtful planning concerns planning in light of cultural differences.
Responsive action concerns adapting behavior when appropriate.
How can Noor present the relationship meaning accurately to Ellis?

A cultural intelligence label guarantees approval of the gift.

intro.heading: Keep the IDC and program application distinct
intro.body:
The official Intercultural Development Continuum names five orientations: Denial, Polarization, Minimization, Acceptance and Adaptation. It concerns increasing complexity in how cultural differences and commonalities are experienced. Its published description of Adaptation connects changing cultural perspective with authentic, culturally appropriate behavior. An ordinary practical adjustment is not automatically that concept.

The example lets you examine a difference between two explanations. Moving a photograph because its caption is too long is an ordinary layout adjustment. Reconsidering how a relationship section honors continuing belonging, then presenting that purpose more accurately to Ellis, connects learned meaning and changed response. This second explanation illustrates the concept for learning. It does not determine Noor’s or Vale’s personal orientation.

The program also uses Integration to mean that the people a process affects help design it; the name comes from Bennett’s developmental model, where it describes identity across cultures. That application is distinct from an added sixth official IDC orientation. A learner should not merge these learning-practice terms, the IDC orientations and the program’s application as though they were one assessment or one sequence. Each has a particular purpose.

You can use the published model to ask whether a learning response genuinely includes cultural meaning rather than only a generic adjustment. You cannot assign a person’s result from a scenario choice, clothing, participation or a preferred layout. Actual IDI assessment and development have their own qualified process. No result is required for access to this practice, and no personnel label belongs in its outcome.

Privately explain what makes the two photograph changes different or consider a meaningful personal perspective shift. The insight may be valuable without a new document or a measured change in agency work. Keep the concept precise and the person unclassified.

lessons.keyStatement: Preserve the model’s meaning without using its names as labels for people in the case.

items.title: Notice what changed in the explanation
items.body: A caption-length change responds to space. Noor’s revised description of relationship sections responds to a newly understood belonging meaning. Both may be useful, but they answer different questions. Naming the cultural meaning prevents every ordinary adjustment from being presented as intercultural adaptation.

items.title: Keep the official sequence accurate
items.body: The published IDC ends in Adaptation among its five named orientations. Program Integration means the people a process affects help design it, and it is identified separately. Preserving that distinction avoids teaching a modified sequence as the provider’s model or implying a new assessment level.

items.title: Do not turn an illustration into a diagnosis
items.body: The example describes a response, not a whole person’s assessed way of experiencing cultural difference. A correct answer cannot supply that missing assessment. Learners can examine the response and improve their understanding without ranking a colleague or making a personal result part of an employee record.

tabs.label: Any change counts as Adaptation
tabs.body: A resized photograph is called proof of IDC Adaptation simply because something changed. This overlooks the model’s cultural perspective-and-behavior meaning. Keep useful practical adjustments recognized without assigning them a concept they do not demonstrate.

tabs.label: A scenario becomes a personal orientation
tabs.body: A learner uses Noor’s revised response to label Noor and compare Vale’s developmental worth. The illustration does not provide an assessment result or a basis for ranking people. Discuss the reasoning and cultural meaning in the response rather than classify the characters.

tabs.label: A precise conceptual comparison
tabs.body: The learner explains the generic layout change, the culturally informed change and the separate program application. This preserves distinctions across concepts. It supports understanding while leaving formal assessment to its actual process and personal insight free from a demanded work result.

check.question: What is the sound conceptual distinction?
check.correct: A cultural meaning informing a suitable response differs from a generic layout adjustment; neither scenario result assesses the person’s IDC orientation.
wrong: Any changed photograph proves the person has an Adaptation orientation.
Program Integration is the sixth official IDC orientation published by the provider.
Motivation and curiosity is another official name for IDC Denial.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The explanation preserves the cultural concept, the five-orientation model and the limit of the example.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A generic layout change does not establish cultural perspective or a personal orientation. Program Integration is identified separately, and These learning practices are not alternate IDC names. Keep the models and their illustrative applications distinct.

Caption spacing responds to a practical layout question.
Noor’s revised account responds to the supplied belonging meaning.
The photograph move establishes Noor’s personal orientation.
Motivation and curiosity is an official IDC orientation.

intro.heading: Keep frameworks alongside evidence and actual responsibilities
intro.body:
Consider a separate DHS team-planning case. Jordan notices that the group’s discussion often favors immediate verbal responses and wonders whether other ways of contributing would help. A cultural framework can suggest examining learned meanings of speaking promptly, considering an idea or showing respect. It cannot determine why any particular colleague is quiet, prove discrimination from that observation alone or authorize Jordan to change a selection requirement.

Jordan could ask an ordinary process question about useful ways to contribute and examine the actual purpose, constraints and available evidence. A colleague may describe a learned meaning, a practical need or a preference, or choose not to supply a personal explanation. A framework should not become a requirement to identify an affiliation before a useful participation method can be considered.

Now add a different fact. Employee Alex tells supervisor Jordan that a coworker repeatedly mocks Alex’s accent and alleges national-origin harassment. This is an actual protected-class allegation in the example, not a reason to assign Alex a communication style. MMB Policy 1436 requires supervisors and managers to immediately report all allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow actual agency procedures. A cultural-framework discussion cannot postpone that responsibility or decide a violation.

DHS equity-analysis responsibilities likewise remain with the actual work. A learning lens may help examine whose perspectives are missing, but it is not a completed formal analysis or authorization for a policy change. Staff can seek program consultation for guidance while keeping appropriate evidence, information handling and responsible roles in place.

Use the full example rather than a live personnel or service account. A sound learning response can distinguish the process question, the allegation and the required responsibilities without scoring anyone’s cultural development.

items.title: Keep a question open to different answers
items.body: Jordan’s observation suggests asking about contribution methods. It does not establish a colleague’s cultural history or motive. A useful response might concern timing, access, meaning or nothing needing change. The framework makes a question visible without supplying the person’s answer.

items.title: Recognize a duty triggered by the actual fact
items.body: Alex explicitly alleges national-origin harassment from repeated accent mockery. Jordan’s immediate reporting responsibility is not conditional on first determining the coworker’s intent or Alex’s cultural style. Actual procedures handle findings; the supervisor follows the required route without using a framework as a delay.

items.title: Preserve evidence and assigned authority
items.body: A proposal about team practice may need actual review, equity analysis or another process within its scope. Conceptual learning does not complete that work or approve a change. Staff can bring clearer questions to the responsible roles while retaining privacy and the evidence the actual decision requires.

tabs.label: A label replaces inquiry
tabs.body: Jordan calls quiet colleagues culturally passive and designs the method around that label. The observation cannot establish the history or preference assigned. It also makes one communication style a verdict about the person. Ask the relevant process question and allow different answers without demanding identity disclosure.

tabs.label: A framework postpones reporting
tabs.body: Jordan offers an informal style workshop before reporting Alex’s allegation. This substitutes learning for the actual immediate duty. An educational lens may support understanding elsewhere, but cannot close, delay or find an outcome for the protected-class complaint.

tabs.label: Inquiry with real responsibilities retained
tabs.body: Jordan examines contribution methods using appropriate accounts and evidence while immediately reporting the separate allegation and following actual procedures. This keeps cultural learning useful without treating it as a substitute decision process or a measure of a person’s worth.

check.question: What should supervisor Jordan do with Alex’s protected-class allegation?
check.correct: Immediately report it to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow actual procedures, without delaying for a framework discussion or making a finding.
wrong: Ask Alex to supply a cultural profile before considering the report.
Complete an informal cultural intelligence exercise first to decide whether reporting is justified.
Promise discipline based on a scenario answer in this course.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The actual reporting duty remains separate from framework learning and a later finding.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A personal cultural profile is not a reporting gate. An informal cultural intelligence exercise cannot determine whether the immediate duty applies to an allegation already raised. Nor can a course answer authorize discipline. Follow the required route and actual procedures without a premature finding.

items.text: Ask which contribution methods would be useful for the team’s purpose.

intro.heading: Choose a useful lens and keep the conclusion proportionate
intro.body:
Ellis considers the memory-book options and chooses accurate captions arranged around several relationships, with a short chronological page at the end. Noor says Vale’s explanation helped reveal why the relationship sections could honor a continuing connection. Vale says Noor’s account helped make the timeline meaningful rather than merely administrative. Those are specific clarified meanings and a particular choice. They do not prove that every recipient prefers this arrangement or that either contributor has a high assessment score.

The frameworks supported different questions. A cultural-meaning lens opened the significance of the order. these learning practices suggested questions about curiosity, understanding, planning and response. The IDC concept helped distinguish culturally informed perspective-and-behavior change from an ordinary layout adjustment. The concepts can complement one another, but their names and purposes are not interchangeable.

A useful summary need not report all frameworks at every step. It might simply explain what the characters learned, which interpretation changed and what Ellis selected. Another project could need a different question or no cultural framework at all. Responsible use is not measured by the number of terms included in an account.

Noor and Vale also understand something about their own ways of honoring a life. That personal insight remains worthwhile if the book is never finished or used at work. A private reflection is not deficient because it does not create a measurable product. You can examine the full example silently and retain whatever meaningful understanding it offers.

Use the job aid as a companion when helpful. Keep the particular account, actual source concepts, remaining uncertainty and responsibilities clear. A lens should support understanding and choice rather than create a new assessment, disclosure expectation or approval gate.

lessons.keyStatement: Keep the framework helpful by saying what it clarified and what remains open.

items.title: Keep the chosen result particular
items.body: Ellis selects one arrangement after hearing the options. That preference belongs to this example. It cannot represent every older neighbor or establish that combining formats is always best. The meaning clarified and choice made are useful without extending them to a population conclusion.

items.title: Select rather than accumulate terminology
items.body: A question about motivation may benefit from motivation and curiosity; a question about individual variation may benefit from the Council of Europe account. Different concepts can serve different inquiries. Including every term does not deepen an explanation if the actual question and evidence are lost.

items.title: Value understanding without a required product
items.body: Noor now sees another expression of regard and Vale recognizes the timeline’s significance. Their own understanding can matter even without a finished book. Recognize that outcome without requiring public cultural notes, a work result or an assessment label as proof.

tabs.label: A combined homemade score
tabs.body: The learner adds these learning practices, IDC names and layout preferences into one cultural-development total. This invents a measure and merges concepts with different purposes. It cannot establish a validated result or justify a personnel decision; keep practice observations and source concepts separate.

tabs.label: More terms as proof of better work
tabs.body: The summary lists every framework but does not explain the changed meaning or Ellis’s choice. The account sounds elaborate while becoming less useful. A short accurate explanation can support deeper understanding than an unexplained collection of labels.

tabs.label: A specific learning account
tabs.body: The learner explains the two learned meanings, the changed interpretations and the recipient’s particular choice, while retaining the model distinctions. Personal understanding remains valid and broader claims remain open. The next step may be private reflection, further practice or appropriate work inquiry.

check.question: What is a sound conclusion from the memory-book follow-up?
check.correct: The characters clarified particular meanings and Ellis made a specific choice; no personal score or universal preference has been established.
wrong: The selected book design proves every recipient prefers relationship sections.
Combining framework names produces a validated cultural score.
The learning is worthless unless the book becomes a measurable agency product.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The conclusion recognizes the actual understanding and choice without an invented measure or required work result.
check.feedbackIncorrect: One choice cannot establish everyone’s preference. Combining distinct names cannot validate a score, and meaningful personal understanding does not depend on an agency product. Keep the particular learning and remaining questions visible.

sections.heading: Hear particular meanings
items: Ask how the relevant act or practice makes sense to this person.
Keep an individual account separate from a community rule or identity prediction.
Check the recipient’s actual preference rather than assume the framework decides it.
Offer private or practice reflection without requiring personal disclosure.

sections.heading: Preserve conceptual distinctions
items: Ask about my own defaults, my team’s norms and what a process assumes, without predicting an individual’s preferences.
Use motivation and curiosity, understanding, Planning and response as distinct learning questions rather than a homemade score.
The official IDC names Denial, Polarization, Minimization, Acceptance and Adaptation; program Integration is separate.
A culturally informed response involves meaning and behavior; an ordinary practical adjustment is not automatically IDC Adaptation.
Do not infer an individual result, reproduce a proprietary assessment or attach a personnel label.

sections.heading: Retain real responsibilities
items: Use actual evidence and assigned review for a service, practice or policy decision; a learning lens is not its completed required analysis.
Supervisors and managers immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow actual agency procedures.
Keep conclusions specific and recognize private personal understanding alongside practical application.
Refer Native American- and Tribal-specific matters to the person or area responsible within ADSA.
